gap_notes: No Layer 2 sign objects yet. motivation / strengths / excess / deficiency / behavioral_tendencies are not 'wrong'; they belong to a later interpretive layer and wait for matching loci. Opened classical divisions (Ptolemy I.14–I.15, I.21; Lilly CA I.16) do not attest them. Do not invent 12 sign objects.

Element conflict: Lilly assigns fire/earth/air/water triplicities. Ptolemy I.21 groups the same four triangles but by winds/directions and planetary lords, not Aristotelian elements on the signs. Do not treat Ptolemy as attesting Aries=fire.

Mode conflict: schema has cardinal|fixed|mutable. Lilly names Aries/Cancer/Libra/Capricorn moveable and cardinal. Ptolemy splits tropical (Cancer, Capricorn) from equinoctial (Aries, Libra). Schema cannot store that split; do not silently collapse Ptolemy into cardinal.
Ptolemy I.15 dismisses quadrupedal/terrestrial/fruitful labels as unimportant. Lilly CA I.16 uses them (e.g. significator in Aries: rash, hardy, lascivious). Not compared.
Individual Lilly sign-nature chapters (body, diseases, places per sign) are not opened this pass. Do not backfill from memory.
CORE cannot be scored for sign meaning packages.

claims.author: Claudius Ptolemy / J.M. Ashmand trans.
claims.locus: Tetrabiblos Book I Chapter XIV (Ashmand p.23)
claims.original_claim: Aries is equinoctial: the first thirty degrees after the vernal equinox, when day and night are equal.
claims.normalized_claim: Aries is equinoctial, not merely 'cardinal' in Ptolemy's vocabulary

claims.author: William Lilly
claims.locus: Book I Chapter XVI Moveable (1659 p.87–88)
claims.original_claim: Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn are moveable and cardinal; from the Sun's entry we name the quarters of the year.
claims.normalized_claim: Lilly classes Aries as moveable and cardinal

claims.author: Claudius Ptolemy / J.M. Ashmand trans.
claims.locus: Tetrabiblos Book I Chapter XV (Ashmand p.23–24)
claims.original_claim: Signs alternate masculine-diurnal and feminine-nocturnal from Aries, which is masculine because the active principle takes precedence.
claims.normalized_claim: Aries is masculine and diurnal; signs then alternate

claims.author: William Lilly
claims.locus: Book I Chapter XVI Masculine (1659 p.87)
claims.original_claim: Masculine diurnal signs, therefore hot: Aries, Gemini, Leo, Libra, Sagittarius, Aquarius; the others feminine nocturnal, therefore cold.
claims.normalized_claim: Aries is masculine and diurnal; signs then alternate

claims.author: Claudius Ptolemy / J.M. Ashmand trans.
claims.locus: Tetrabiblos Book I Chapter XXI (Ashmand p.29–30)
claims.original_claim: Aries, Leo, Sagittarius form the first triplicity; lords Sun and Jupiter; principally northern by Jupiter's airy winds, also north-west by Mars.
claims.normalized_claim: Ptolemy's Aries-Leo-Sagittarius triangle is a wind/direction triplicity

claims.author: William Lilly
claims.locus: Book I Chapter XVI Elements (1659 p.87)
claims.original_claim: Aries, Leo, Sagittarius are fiery, hot and dry, and constitute the fiery triplicity.
claims.normalized_claim: Lilly's Aries-Leo-Sagittarius triangle is the fiery element

claims.author: Claudius Ptolemy / J.M. Ashmand trans.
claims.locus: Tetrabiblos Book I Chapter XIV (Ashmand p.23)
claims.original_claim: Fixed signs immediately follow tropical and equinoctial signs; the season's quality is then more firmly established.
claims.normalized_claim: Fixed signs confirm the season begun in the preceding turning sign

claims.author: William Lilly
claims.locus: Book I Chapter XVI Fixed (1659 p.88)
claims.original_claim: Fixed signs follow the equinoctial and tropics: Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius; the season is then fixed.
claims.normalized_claim: Fixed signs confirm the season begun in the preceding turning sign

claims.author: Claudius Ptolemy / J.M. Ashmand trans.
claims.locus: Tetrabiblos Book I Chapter XIV (Ashmand p.23)
claims.original_claim: Bicorporeal signs follow the fixed and participate in both the fixed and the tropical constitutions.
claims.normalized_claim: Bicorporeal/common signs partake of both neighbouring constitutions

claims.author: William Lilly
claims.locus: Book I Chapter XVI Common (1659 p.88)
claims.original_claim: Common signs sit between moveable and fixed: Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces; they partake of both, and are bicorporeal.
claims.normalized_claim: Bicorporeal/common signs partake of both neighbouring constitutions
